title: id(local_claims): hex_bytes is the one pkgs/id hex parser the #2517 gate missed — it panics on misaligned multi-byte input and accepts '+'-pair spellings

body:
## Summary

`pkgs/id/src/local_claims.rs`'s private `hex_bytes` (lines 247–257) is the one hex parser in pkgs/id that the #2517/#3457 hardening missed: it has no ASCII-hexdigit gate and decodes by slicing `&text[index..index + 2]` at byte offsets. Two consequences, both verified this run on main `4af4ee8354`:

1. **Panic instead of the designed error.** A `local-claims.jsonl` line whose `id`/`author`/`subject` field has even byte length but contains a multi-byte character at a misaligned offset panics with `byte index 2 is not a char boundary` instead of returning the function's `"{text:?} is not hex"` error. `LocalClaims::open` (local_claims.rs:69–97) is explicitly built to turn a malformed line into an `InvalidData` io error naming the file and line number; the panic escapes that handling and crashes the caller (`LocalEvents` open at local_events.rs:233) on a corrupt/hand-edited/sync-mangled claims file.
2. **Non-canonical `+` spellings accepted.** `u8::from_str_radix` accepts a leading `+`, so `"+a"` decodes as `0x0a` — exactly the dual-spelling problem #2517 fixed in `directory.rs::hex_to_array` and `directory_auth.rs::hex_bytes`, and that `invites/invitation.rs::parse_hex32` and `seitan/derive.rs::InviteId::from_hex` also gate against. Every sibling parser gates on `bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit())` first; this one does not.

## Evidence

- `pkgs/id/src/local_claims.rs:247-257` — ungated slicing decoder (only guard is an even-length check).
- Sibling gates for comparison: `pkgs/id/src/directory.rs:2597-2610`, `pkgs/id/src/directory_auth.rs:370-385`, `pkgs/id/src/invites/invitation.rs:124-135`, `pkgs/id/src/seitan/derive.rs:66-76`.
- Probe (laptop, `~/git/fleet/probe-localclaims-hex`, exact copy of the function, main `4af4ee8354`):
  - `hex_bytes(&"0a".repeat(32))` → `Ok([10, …])` (control)
  - `hex_bytes(&"zz".repeat(32))` → `Err("… is not hex")` (control)
  - `hex_bytes(&"+a".repeat(32))` → `Ok([10, …])` (non-canonical spelling accepted)
  - `hex_bytes("€a")` (4 bytes, even) → **PANIC** `end byte index 2 is not a char boundary; it is inside '€' (bytes 0..3)`

## Why it matters

The claims file is on-disk state read at open time; robustness there is the difference between a named, line-numbered error and an unexplained crash. The missing gate is also a consistency hole in a hardening pass (#2517/#3457) that was supposed to cover the repo's hex decoders.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `hex_bytes` in `local_claims.rs` refuses any input containing a non-ASCII-hexdigit byte (including `+`-pairs) with the existing `is not hex` error, mirroring the #2517 sibling gates.
- [ ] No input to `hash_from_hex`/`author_from_hex` can panic: decoding works on bytes (e.g. `as_bytes().chunks(2)` + `from_utf8`) or is fully gated before slicing.
- [ ] New unit tests in `local_claims.rs` cover: a `+`-pair input, a multi-byte-character input of even byte length (misaligned), and the existing valid/odd-length/non-hex cases.
- [ ] `cargo test -p id local_claims` passes.
